title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
authors: NeoHorse Team: 36 authors listed alphabetically (18 core contributors, 18 contributors); corresponding authors Yu Wang and Yunhe Wang
lab: TokenRhythm Technologies, with Infinigence AI, Tsinghua University, Peking University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Alibaba Group, Visionplus Capital and WX Capital
date: 8 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version so far)

code.title: weights only, Apache 2.0
code.note: The repository holds the README, the report's PDF, two inference examples (chat and tool calls) and the later NeoHorse-Jev decision model. The 4B and 9B checkpoints are on Hugging Face (text-only BF16 weights, the vision tower of Qwen3.5 removed) with GGUF quantisations. No training code, curation pipeline, router, curriculum scores or training data are released

takeaway: Makes the serving harness the source of the training curriculum rather than downstream infrastructure: a router over a heterogeneous model pool predicts each request's capability demand, those routing signals order a three-stage SFT curriculum, interactions become training data through structural validation plus six-dimensional semantic evaluation plus subscene-level labelling, a teacher supervises the student's own responses (on-policy distillation) under the same progression, and evaluation feedback feeds back into the training mixture; the macro-average across ten agent, tool-use, coding and instruction benchmarks goes 58.94 to 64.87 at 4B and 65.60 to 69.04 at 9B, with the post-trained 4B closing 89% of the macro gap to the base 9B.
verdict: Believe that this post-training made Qwen3.5-4B and 9B better agents: the 4B improves on all ten benchmarks, and the HumanEval and VitaBench gains are three standard errors clear of sampling noise. Do not read it as evidence for the routing ideas or for recursive self-improvement: no experiment turns the routing curriculum, the on-policy distillation or the allocation step off, the loop ran once, and the one controlled experiment's "+6.26 over public data" is mostly the public-data run falling 4.99 points below the untrained model.

headline.k: Qwen3.5-4B before and after NeoHorse-1 post-training, over ten benchmarks; up on all ten
headline.d: 9B: 65.60 → 69.04, up on 7, level on 2, down on 1

headline.k: the public-data (Toucan) run against the untrained base on the five benchmarks of the data comparison; the routing-harness run is +1.26
headline.d: the paper prints the +6.26 between them, not the base

headline.k: evaluation, selection and update ran once; whether gains compound across iterations is untested, as the authors say
headline.d: the RSI claim is a design, not a measurement

resources.t: Agentic Routing: The Harness-Native Data Flywheel
resources.n: the companion paper NeoHorse-1 builds on: the step-level router, the four-pass OpenSquilla routing stack (admission, demand construction, risk pricing, capability matching with an open LightGBM ranker), and the argument that every routing decision is a labelled training record.
the open agent harness used to evaluate QwenClawBench and PinchBench here, with the cold-start router; the closest thing to the paper's harness that anyone outside the company can run.
the released weights (Apache 2.0, text only), the SGLang and vLLM recipes and the evaluation tables; the 9B card is in the same collection.

resources.t: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
resources.n: the method §4.3 extends: the student samples, the teacher scores every token of the student's own response, and a divergence such as reverse KL is minimised on those prefixes.
the clearest explanation of why on-policy distillation is dense like supervised learning but on the student's own states like RL, with per-token reverse KL as the reward; the background to Eq. 3.

resources.t: TOUCAN: Synthesizing 1.5M Tool-Agentic Data from Real-World MCP Environments
resources.n: the public dataset Table 3 compares against; worth reading before trusting that comparison, since how a public set is sampled and serialised decides how it does in someone else's recipe.

resources.t: Co-Harness: Co-evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
resources.n: the closest related work the paper cites: harness and weights updated jointly, rather than the harness only supplying data.

resources.t: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL
resources.n: keeps the RL environment loop inside the deployment harness: the RL counterpart of NeoHorse-1's supervised and distillation recipe.

kb.n: the issue that covered this paper (Research and papers, with 412 Hugging Face upvotes at the time) next to MOLE and Φ-Bench; its check accepted the arXiv listing's "eleven benchmarks", which the paper's own tables put at ten.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: the other half of the loop: models building and evolving the harness rather than the harness training the model; its finding that visible gains moved with held-out gains only about half the time is the warning for any self-improvement loop judged on its own feedback.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: found that rich harnesses offer affordances models are not trained to use; NeoHorse-1 is one answer, training on the harness's own traffic.

kb.t: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
kb.n: trained a model to emit harnesses, but in a language far poorer than a production one; NeoHorse-1 trains inside a production harness instead.

kb.t: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
kb.n: supplies the environments; NeoHorse-1 supplies the trajectories from live traffic instead of synthesised tasks.

kb.t: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
kb.n: supplies skills mined from repositories; together with Terminal-Universe and this paper, three different feeds into an agent's training.

kb.t: Φ-Bench: Can Large Language Models Engineer the Infrastructure That Powers Them?
kb.n: measures whether a model can build its own infrastructure and finds it mostly cannot; NeoHorse-1's loop keeps humans building the infrastructure and lets the model only learn from it.

kb.t: MOLE: Detecting Insider Threats in AI Agents
kb.n: asks what a loop like this does when it is subverted: an agent inside the organisation whose traffic becomes the next model's training data.

kb.t: Learn What's Left, Not What's Mastered (SA-MRPO)
kb.n: saturation-aware reweighting of RL training objectives: the same shape as capability-guided allocation (spend data where the model is still weak), arrived at from the training side.

kb.t: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
kb.n: a later recursive self-improvement loop in which the environments evolve with the agent.

kb.t: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
kb.n: regularises a harness self-improvement loop against overfitting its own feedback, the failure mode a multi-pass NeoHorse loop would have to guard against.
the iterative SFT, rejection sampling and DPO recipe with synthetic multi-step tool-use data that §2.1 names as the trajectory-SFT baseline approach.

topics.n: the harness-scaling section: this paper is the sixth strategy there, the first where the harness is a training-data source rather than a runtime wrapper.
subscene-level labelling and routing-derived curricula belong next to the distillation and curriculum material, and next to the data-against-model efficiency decomposition filed there.
capability-guided allocation as an allocation policy over training data, beside SA-MRPO's reweighting; on-policy distillation as the dense-reward cousin of RL.
the ten benchmarks, several of them built around one harness family (OpenClaw), and how few items some of them have.
